title: Nervous system: female anatomy
description: Female nervous-system overview with focused pelvic nerve notes for uterus, vagina, clitoris and vulva; tiny branches are not falsely pinned.

questions.question: Is the female nervous system built differently from the male nervous system?
questions.answer: The central and most peripheral pathways share the same basic organization. A female-focused pelvic view discusses branches serving the uterus, vagina, clitoris and vulva without implying a separate female brain or spinal cord.

questions.question: What carries sensation from the clitoral glans?
questions.answer: The dorsal nerve of the clitoris, a terminal branch of the pudendal nerve, conveys much of the somatic sensation. Autonomic nerves influence erectile tissues but should not be confused with that sensory pathway.

questions.question: Which nerves supply the vulva and lower vagina?
questions.answer: Pudendal branches supply much of the posterior vulva and lower vaginal region. The anterior labia also receive contributions from ilioinguinal and genitofemoral branches, so a single nerve label cannot cover the entire area.

questions.question: What is the uterovaginal plexus?
questions.answer: It is an autonomic network associated with the cervix and upper vagina that carries branches toward the uterus and upper vagina. It is anatomically distinct from the superficial pudendal branches of the perineum.

questions.question: Does the full-body female nerve plate identify tiny pelvic branches?
questions.answer: No. The full-body plate is for orientation to larger pathways. Tiny pelvic autonomic and sensory branches are explained in study entries without pretending they can be seen or precisely localized on this image.
